say:1:1041580401:1.text: Ah, a survivor of the battlefield... Your soul is remarkably resilient.
say:1:1041580401:1.source_cn: 啊，一位战场幸存者，有着无比坚韧的灵魂。

say:3:1041580403:1.text: Heh. I take it you've met those warmongers.
say:3:1041580403:1.source_cn: 呵呵，看来你认识那群战争狂。

say:4:1041580404:1.text: Don't worry. I'm nothing like them. If they had even half my common sense, I wouldn't have had to move so many times.
say:4:1041580404:1.source_cn: 放心，我和他们不同。但凡他们有我一半的理智，我也不至于...

say:5:1041580405:1.text: I have no quarrel with the living. You can lower your weapon.
say:5:1041580405:1.source_cn: 我无意与生者争斗，你可以放下武器。

say:6:1041580406:1.text: You don't give the orders here, Graveborn.

say:7:1041580407:1.text: That tone takes me back. You must have served in the military, and you've crossed blades with Bantus before.
say:7:1041580407:1.source_cn: 真是令人怀念的语气。你一定在军队待过，而且曾经和班题斯交手。

say:8:1041580408:1.text: Your posture, your footwork, the look in your eye, that sharp instinct... Interesting. You're still in remarkably good condition.
say:8:1041580408:1.source_cn: 站姿、步态、眼神，还有下意识的警惕……你还是最出色的那类。

say:10:1041580410:1.text: Something like that. I was a field medic when I was alive. Saved plenty of people like you. Others... didn't make it.
say:10:1041580410:1.source_cn: 姑且算是吧。我生前是个军医，救过很多像你这样的人。当然...

say:11:1041580411:1.text: ... That's war for you. But you don't sound like you've made peace with it.
say:11:1041580411:1.source_cn: ……战场之事向来如此。但听你的口气，不像是释怀了。

say:12:1041580412:1.text: Death doesn't bring only eternal peace. Sometimes, it leaves you with an eternity of questions.
say:12:1041580412:1.source_cn: 毕竟死后不只有永恒的宁静，还有无尽的烦恼。

say:13:1041580413:1.text: Wounds of the soul are considerably harder to heal than wounds of the flesh. The interesting thing is, the dead often leave behind more mysteries than the living.
say:13:1041580413:1.source_cn: 灵魂创伤比肉体病痛更难治愈。到头来，亡者身上的谜团竟比...

say:14:1041580414:1.text: Still, you needn't worry. At least emotions tend to stay quite stable once you're dead.
say:14:1041580414:1.source_cn: 不过你无须担心，至少人死后的情绪会很稳定。

say:15:1041580415:1.text: I will never become a Graveborn. But my friend...
say:15:1041580415:1.source_cn: 我绝不会变成亡灵。但我的朋友……

say:16:1041580416:1.text: Turned into one? What a shame.
say:16:1041580416:1.source_cn: 变成亡灵了？真是遗憾啊。

say:17:1041580417:1.text: But if you truly can't let them go, wouldn't becoming a Graveborn and staying by their side forever be the better choice? Ah, not now, of course. I mean someday.
say:17:1041580417:1.source_cn: 不过，如果你真的放不下他，变成亡灵和他永远作伴难道不是...

say:18:1041580418:1.text: ... I told you. I'll never become a Graveborn.

say:19:1041580419:1.text: If the situation hadn't been so dire, if there had been any other choice... I never would've wanted my friend to become a Graveborn, either.
say:19:1041580419:1.source_cn: 如果不是当时情况紧急，如果不是没有选择……我也不想他变...

say:20:1041580420:1.text: But what's done is done, and none of us can rewrite the past, can we?
say:20:1041580420:1.source_cn: 但事情已经发生，谁都无力改变，不是吗？

say:21:1041580421:1.text: If you ask me, spending eternity with your loved ones, even as a Graveborn, can be a beautiful life in its own way.
say:21:1041580421:1.source_cn: 如果要我来说，与家人永远相伴——哪怕是以亡灵的身份——...

say:22:1041580422:1.text: ... Thank you for the advice, but I hope I'll never need it.
say:22:1041580422:1.source_cn: ……感谢你的劝告，但我更希望我用不上。

say:23:1041580423:1.text: If you can hold on to who you are, becoming a Graveborn might have its advantages. But most of the ones I've encountered have been used by others to commit terrible acts.
say:23:1041580423:1.source_cn: 如果能维持自我，变成亡灵或许有好处。可惜的是，我见过的...

say:24:1041580424:1.text: I know my friend won't become like that. But I don't want to risk becoming that way myself.
say:24:1041580424:1.source_cn: 我相信我的朋友不会变成那副模样，但我也不希望我有变成那...
